facts.field: Malcolm Gladwell's perspective on social media and activism
facts.value: Malcolm Gladwell considers the role of social media in revolutions and protests to be overstated. He concluded that while social media makes it easier for activists to express themselves, that expression likely has no impact beyond social media.
facts.programme_association: Social Sciences - BSc | University of Limerick

facts.value: High-risk activism involves strong relationships, coordination, commitment, high risks, and sacrifice.
facts.programme_association: Social Sciences - BSc | University of Limerick

facts.value: Gladwell claims that social media are built around weak ties and argues that social networks are effective at increasing participation by lessening the level of motivation that participation requires.
facts.programme_association: Social Sciences - BSc | University of Limerick

facts.field: impact of Facebook activism according to Gladwell
facts.value: According to him, Facebook activism succeeds not by motivating people to make a real sacrifice, but by motivating them to do the things that people do when they are not motivated enough to make a real sacrifice.
facts.programme_association: Social Sciences - BSc | University of Limerick

facts.value: A 2018 survey reported that people who are politically expressive on social media are more likely to participate in offline political activity.
